exceptions.reason: Next.js 14.2.35 contains known advisories affecting image optimization and App Router cache handling. Patched in 15.5.25+ / 15.5.28+ which requires React 19 and breaking async request APIs.
exceptions.exploitability: Low in RESOLVE-ONE: remote image optimization is restricted to trusted origins, App Router routes enforce Cache-Control: no-store, and server actions are not used for privileged mutations.
compensatingControls: No-store cache directives on authenticated routes
Strict Content-Security-Policy with isolated frame-ancestors
Input schemas strictly bound by Zod before processing

advisoryDetails.title: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections

exceptions.reason: Zod < 4.6.6 memory exhaustion when validating unbounded collection constraints. Fix requires Zod 4.x which introduces breaking API changes.
exceptions.exploitability: Low in RESOLVE-ONE: all HTTP request bodies are hard-capped at 1MB by Next.js / Edge runtime, preventing transmission of massive collections before Zod validation executes.
compensatingControls: JSON payload size restricted to 1MB at server gateway
Array fields in schemas have explicit small lengths
Distributed rate limiter throttles incoming requests per IP/account

DOMPurify: FORBID_TAGS bypassed by function-based ADD_TAGS predicate (asymmetry with FORBID_ATTR fix)
DOMPurify has a SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES bypass in RETURN_DOM mode

DOMPurify: IN_PLACE mode preserves attributes of a clobbered root element, allowing XSS via attacker-controlled root DOM
DOMPurify IN_PLACE Sanitization Bypass via Attached Shadow Root Inside <template>.content
DOMPurify: Permanent `ALLOWED_ATTR` pollution via `setConfig()` bypassing the hook clone-guard (incomplete fix of the 3.4.7 hook-pollution patch)
DOMPurify: Trusted Types policy survives `clearConfig()` and can poison later `RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE` output
DOMPurify: `IN_PLACE` mode trusts attacker-controlled `nodeName` on live non-form nodes, allowing script retention and XSS via attacker-supplied DOM objects
DOMPurify: Hook mutation of `data.allowedTags` / `data.allowedAttributes` permanently pollutes `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TAGS` / `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ATTR`
DOMPurify's ADD_TAGS function form bypasses FORBID_TAGS due to short-circuit evaluation
DOMPurify ADD_ATTR predicate skips URI validation
DOMPurify USE_PROFILES prototype pollution allows event handlers

DOMPurify: IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS
DOMPurify: `CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING` bypasses `afterSanitizeElements` for allowed custom elements.
DOMPurify: IN_PLACE returns a force-removed rawtext root whose text carries attacker markup — pure HTML reparse executes
DOMPurify IN_PLACE: hook that removes a parent or sibling leaves the detached subtree's event handlers armed (incomplete fix for GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
DOMPurify: SMIL attributeName=href guard is skipped when PARSER_MEDIA_TYPE is application/xhtml+xml

exceptions.reason: DOMPurify is pulled as a transitive dependency of jspdf for SVG rendering. Resolved at 2.5.9. Direct input sanitization in Resolve uses sanitizeHtml string sanitizers.
exceptions.exploitability: Negligible: RESOLVE-ONE does not execute raw HTML from untrusted users and disables SVG script execution in jspdf.
compensatingControls: Client-side PDF generation only operates on sanitized text strings
DOMPurify RETURN_DOM mode is never invoked in Resolve codebase

exceptions.reason: Development server CORS request handling vulnerability in esbuild <= 0.24.2. Transitive dependency of Vite dev server.
exceptions.exploitability: None in production: esbuild is purely a dev/test build tool and is never deployed or executed in production.
compensatingControls: Strict separation of dev dependencies from production build artifacts
Dev server only runs on local loopback interface with no external network exposure

exceptions.reason: Nested dependency of Next.js 14.2.35 (node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss @ 8.4.31). Upstream update linked to Next.js 15 upgrade.
exceptions.exploitability: None in production runtime: PostCSS is executed exclusively during Next.js build-time CSS compilation, not on dynamic user input at runtime.
compensatingControls: Build pipeline only processes local, trusted repository stylesheets
Source maps are disabled or isolated in production build output
